title: Why Dropshipping Won't Make You Rich (Even With Sales)
alts: The Real Cost of Running a Dropshipping Store (With Numbers)
I Made $3,000 in Sales and Lost $1,546 — Here's Why
line1: Dave made $3,000 in sales his first month dropshipping. His bank account went DOWN $1,546. We follow every dollar.
summary: Dave opens a dropshipping store on Shopify selling a $30 glowing cat lamp that costs him $12. Eighteen dollars profit per lamp sounds great on paper. But after payment fees, Facebook ads at fifty cents per click with a two percent buy rate, twenty refunds when lamps take too long to arrive, and two chargebacks, Dave's first month ends at minus one thousand five hundred forty six dollars on three thousand dollars of sales. The villain: everyone who gets paid whether the store wins or loses. Meta made fifty nine billion in ad revenue in one quarter. Shopify's payment side brought in two point seven eight billion. The supplier gets paid up front. Dave takes all the risk. The one number he should have checked first: his ad ceiling. Thirty dollars minus twelve minus fees leaves sixteen eighty. If ads cost more than that per customer, every sale loses money. Dave was paying twenty five dollars in ads per lamp. Scaling a loss just multiplies it. He closes the store and month two's damage never happens. Some people build real online businesses, usually with their own product or skill, not the same lamp as ten thousand other stores.
